- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods of the 30-day forecast, especially after sharp spikes or volatility.
- Overestimates near the end of the forecast horizon, particularly in the last 5–7 days, suggesting lag or delayed response to recent price trends.
- Shows persistent bias toward lower values when historical mean is high (e.g., 60+), indicating underconfidence in upward momentum.
- Tends to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 65+), then corrects with a downward bias — suggesting model overreacts to short-term volatility.
- Mean reversion is implied: forecasts often settle near historical average (55–60) after initial over/underestimation, but not always captured in early days.
- Horizon-specific: last 5–7 days of forecast are more volatile and less accurate, suggesting model struggles with short-term price dynamics or lacks recent data weighting.
- Avoids extreme outliers in forecast — tends to smooth out sharp moves, even when true price spikes or drops occur.
